title: Faces under continuous flash suppression capture attention faster than objects, but without a face evoked steady-state visual potential: Is curvilinearity responsible for the behavioral effect?
research_question: Does face processing occur without conscious awareness, and if so, is the behavioral advantage for faces due to mid-level visual features like curvilinearity rather than high-level category membership?

participants.description: Study 1: 25 participants (11 men, 14 women, median age 21). Study 2: 24 participants (7 men, 17 women, median age 21). Study 3: 35 participants (12 men, 25 women, median age 21). All had normal or corrected-to-normal vision, recruited from Kenyon College campus and surrounding community.
participants.recruitment: Recruited from the Kenyon College campus and surrounding community and compensated for their participation.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Greyscale, 200x200 jpeg images (72 pixels/inch), mean luminance matched (M=135, SD=45), with a cyan filter. Presented using red-cyan anaglyph glasses. Continuous flash suppression (CFS) mask was a 20x20 matrix of 20px² cells, re-randomized every 166.67ms. Images presented at 6 Hz, with oddball stimuli presented every fifth image (1.2 Hz). Stimuli included: neutral faces (MR2 Face Database), fearful faces (Averaged Karolinska Directed Emotional Faces), common objects (Brady et al., 2008), curvilinear objects (e.g., dartboard), rectilinear objects (e.g., chessboard), and scrambled objects.

measures.construct: Breakthrough time of suppressed images into conscious awareness
measures.instrument: Participant button press indicating awareness; calculated as (maximum run duration - actual run duration). Larger value indicates faster breakthrough.
Steady-state visually evoked potentials (SSVEP) at the oddball presentation frequency (1.2 Hz) and its harmonics, recorded from 64 scalp electrodes (ROI: P8, PO8, P10).

mechanisms: Mid-level visual features, specifically curvilinearity, are responsible for the faster breakthrough time of faces and curvilinear objects under continuous flash suppression, rather than high-level category membership.
Curvilinear contours are preferentially processed in the central visual field and show increasing preference from lower to higher visual processing areas.
Human face-selective regions are particularly sensitive to curvilinearity.
An intriguing relationship exists between curvilinearity and animacy, where animate things tend to be more curvilinear.
limitations: Low opacity images were used to extend suppression time, which might account for the inability to detect an EEG response, though behavioral effects were still observed.
Faces were a more homogeneous set of stimuli than objects, potentially facilitating faster breakthrough due to repetition of homogeneous oddballs.
The curvilinearity effect might be due to contrast with rectilinear CFS stimuli, as no condition included curvilinear CFS masks.
The data cannot rule out subcortical nonconscious processing of fearful faces.
The data cannot speak to the importance of convexity vs. concavity, only curvilinear over rectilinear contours.
